ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $2.44 voucher refund to the rider for the unexempted off-route segment (RydeTAXI metered excess), and issue the driver a coaching notice for breaching the shortest-and-most-direct-route obligation (RD-1); do not refund the remainder of the trip distance.

segment_findings.reason: Off-route segment 17:41–17:44, 1.73 km extra, up to 979 m from the optimal route. No exemption: RD-4(a) fails because the accident in [F12] was located 0 m from the optimal route rather than on the substituted stretch, and RD-4(b) band evidence (Seletar Expressway band 4, [F10]) cannot exempt a segment alone; RD-5 fails because no driver request for the route change preceded the segment and no rider agreement exists ([F7][F8]); RD-3 fails because no rider-named stop or edit-destination request preceded the segment ([F7]). Refundable under RD-2: 1.73 km × $1.4102/km = $2.44 [RD-1][RD-2][RD-3][RD-4][RD-5].

rejected_claims.reason: The whole-trip gross figure (+2.1 km, +12%, [F1]) is not itself the refundable amount: RD-2 refunds only the extra_km of unexempted segments and expressly excludes the non-segment residual, so the trip total does not establish a refund beyond the single segment in [F3] [RD-2].

Partly rejected: the $2.90 figure taken from [F4] (2.1 km × $1.41/km) double-counts the ~0.37 km residual not attributable to any off-route segment; RD-2 computes the refund as segment extra_km × (distance_fare ÷ distance_km), i.e. 1.73 km, not the 2.1 km whole-trip excess [F1][F3][F4][RD-2].

Rejected as framed: the rider's own reading of [F10] (Seletar Expressway at band 4, the road the driver says he used, [F9]) is not the ground of decision; the segment is denied exemption because [F12]'s accident lay 0 m from the optimal route rather than on the substituted stretch, and band evidence alone cannot exempt under RD-4(b) [F10][F12][RD-4].

Rejected: the rider's dispute history ([F14]) is profile material and cannot decide the case; the outcome rests on the segment findings in [F3] and the RD-2 rate, not on the rider's record [F14][RD-2].

Accepted in part but insufficient for the driver: the existence of a single 1.73 km off-route segment [F3] is exactly what triggers RD-1 liability and a RD-2 refund, so it fails to support the requested no_action [F3][RD-1].

Rejected: the RD-4 exemption is not established on the record — the accident in [F12] sat 0 m from the optimal route (not the replaced stretch) and RD-4(b) band evidence cannot exempt alone ([F10]); RD-5's silence on consent does not supply the missing traffic condition [F10][F12][RD-4][RD-5].

Rejected as a bar to refund: the disclosure of fare components ([F5][F6]) is uncontested, but RD-2 makes the extra kilometres of an unexempted metered segment refundable regardless of correct component disclosure, and [F3] is such a segment [F3][F6][RD-2].
The no-flag point is accepted (0 upheld route disputes in 90 days, [F15]), but it does not defeat the refund; RD-6 governs only the additional account action, not this case's outcome [F15][RD-6].
